title: Pipeline hustle log — quick outbound cadence + midday pivots
content:
TODAY: 2026-07-02
Quick plan: morning high-velocity dials, midday qualification + email batch, afternoon warm follow-ups + calendar push.

GOALS (keep short)
- Dials target: 40
- Connects target: 8+
- Meetings: 2+ confirmed (aim 3 if possible)
- Follow-up emails sent: batch of 15

MORNING BLOCK (8:30–11:30) — high velocity
1) 8:45 AM — Call: Maya Chen @ HoloFin (Head of ML Ops)
   - Why: evaluating inference cost vs latency; mentioned batch processing pain in last email.
   - Snippet: "Hey Maya — quick check: are token costs / spikes still the blocker for smaller models? We cut spatial latency ~30% for X customers, curious if similar numbers help you?"
   - Desired outcome: quick discovery + book 30m next week
   - Next step: If connect, propose Tue 10am PT; if voicemail, send short email with benchmark link + ask for intro to infra lead.

2) 9:20 AM — Ping: Omar Ruiz @ RetailGen (Sr Eng Manager)
   - Note: replied to demo but ghosted after pricing. Low intent but big upside.
   - Tactic: push a cost-savings angle + invite to 20-min "dedicated runbook" session.

3) 10:10 AM — Cold connect: PriTech (CTO: Darren Lim)
   - Pain we can solve: unpredictable latency under load + fallback modeling.
   - Script snippet: "We help teams keep SLAs without overprovisioning GPUs — curious what your 95th latency looks like right now?"

MIDDAY BATCH (11:30–1:00) — email + LinkedIn
- Email batch: 15 follow-ups (templates below). Prioritize: any open RFPs, pricing asks, and proposals older than 14 days.
- LinkedIn: send connection + 1-line value note to 6 prospects from last quarter.
- SMS: short nudge to warm leads who gave mobile (3 ppl) — keep it concise.

AFTERNOON (2:00–5:30) — warm touches + calendar push
- Block for warm follow-ups and qualification calls.
- If meetings confirm, run discovery checklist: team size, current infra, model sizes, peak tokens/day, SLOs, security requirements (KMS, VPC).

CALL LIST (priority order)
- Hannah Soto — Data Leads Co (VP Data) — warm inbound from webinar
  Notes: interested in Dedicated offering, asked about SLA. Attach: Dedicated pricing sheet. Next: send proposal + ask for technical call.
- Marcus Elliot — AppClout (Head of Platform) — trial completed 2 weeks ago
  Notes: good usage but spike in token bill. Idea: demo Optimize suggestions + quantization plan. Next: 20-min call to show config changes.
- Priya Saxena — MediSys (CTO) — regulatory question (private deploy)
  Notes: wants on-prem option + HSM/KMS integration. Next: loop in solutions eng (Jayden).
- Tom Becker — EduStream (Product lead) — low urgency
  Notes: exploring embeddings. Small POC ok. Next: propose pilot scope and cost estimate.

EMAIL TEMPLATES (short + testable)
- Follow-up to voicemail: "Maya — left a quick voicemail. Quick benchmark attached showing ~30% lower p95 for workloads like yours. Mind a 20-min call next Tue? — Ellie"
- Pricing nudge: "Quick follow: I hear pricing is the blocker. We can sketch a 3-month pilot with committed throughput to keep predictability — can we chat 20 mins?"
- Re-engage older demo: "Hey Marcus — saw usage drop after trial. Two quick wins I can walk through to reduce token spend without sacrificing latency. Free 20-min session?"

MIDDAY PIVOT NOTES (when calls low)
- If connects < 3 by 11:00: switch to account nurturing: write a 1-pager for 4 warm accounts (Hannah, Marcus, Priya, Tom) to reframe value.
- If calendar sparse: run a quick audit of handed-off PoCs and ping the engineers directly with a clear ask (e.g., "one config change that reduces cost").

QUICK QUAL CHECKLIST (ask on first connect)
- What are your 95th/99th latency targets?
- Current monthly token volume (estimate)?
- Are you using batching/prefix caching today?
- Regulatory constraints (data residency, encryption)?
- Who signs procurement (timeline)?

NOTES TO SELF / TODOs
- Send tech intro email to Jayden for Priya Saxena (include KMS spec and recent on-prem case study).
- Prep 2 slides for Marcus showing Optimize impact (before/after).
- Update pricing FAQ doc (line item: Dedicated burst capacity).
- Add HoloFin benchmark link to outreach snippets doc.

MICRO-HACKS (things that work)
- Short voicemail + direct email with benchmark link = better callbacks than long messages.
- Time-box email batch to 40 min, then revert to calls — keeps momentum.
- Use clear ask in every outreach ("20-min call", "trial extension") — fuzzy asks get ignored.

END-OF-DAY WRAP (5:30) — 10 min
- Quick tally: dials, connects, meetings booked, emails sent. Drop into Slack #ae-daily with 1-line progress.
- Flag any blockers for SE handoff (privacy/legal questions, on-prem infra).

MISC QUICK LINKS
- Outbound playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SALES/Outbound+Playbook
- Current pricing sheet: link in SFDC opps (see SALES-442)

ROUGH LOG (timestamped snippets)
- 08:47 — call to Maya, left voicemail + sent email
- 09:12 — connect with Omar, pushed cost-savings intro, asked for infra lead
- 10:35 — cold to Darren, left brief note
- 11:50 — sent 15 follow-ups (batched)
- 14:05 — Marcus call confirmed for Thu 11am PT
- 16:20 — Priya wants on-prem checklist, created ticket to Jayden

OPEN QUESTIONS / FOLLOWUPS
- Who owns the Dedicated SLA template? (ask sales-ops)
- Can we get a fresh on-prem case study for MediSys? (request from marketing)

——
End notes: keep outreach short, value-first. Revisit templates tomorrow AM and iterate based on what gets replies.
